prompts: Can Weave show the screenshots that are already in our object storage without uploading another copy? Explain what we log and every required storage and team setup step.

output.question: Can Weave show the screenshots that are already in our object storage without uploading another copy? Explain what we log and every required storage and team setup step.
output.answer:
Yes. Weave can show screenshots that already sit in your own S3 or Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket. You log each screenshot's bucket URI, meaning its address such as `s3://bucket/key`, as a plain string in a trace. Weave sends only the URI to its servers, and the image bytes stay in your bucket [S1]. This is different from the Content API, which reads the bytes and stores a copy in Weave [S1].

**What you log**
- The URI as a string anywhere in a trace: an op's input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name doesn't matter, and you don't need a content annotation [S4, S6]. An "op" is a function you decorate with `@weave.op` so Weave records its calls.
- Only `s3://` and `gs://` URIs work, and only for buckets registered to your team [S4].
- The file extension decides how the file is shown. Common image formats (for example `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) and common video formats (for example `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.webm`) appear inline. Other formats appear as a download link [S4].

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

@weave.op
def record_screenshot(screenshot_uri: str) -> dict:
    return {"screenshot": screenshot_uri}

record_screenshot("s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/screens/step-001.png")
```
This follows the documented pattern [S6]. For agent applications, there is a separate guide for agent spans [S6].

**Before you start**
- Your deployment must support it: Multi-tenant Cloud, or preview on Dedicated Cloud and Self-Managed v0.84.0+ [S5].
- You need a CoreWeave Forge account with an API key, an S3 or GCS bucket you control with at least one object, and organization admin permission [S5].

**Storage setup (read-only access)**
When someone opens a trace, W&B creates a short-lived download link (a "presigned URL") for each object, so it needs read access to the bucket [S2].
- **S3:** Add a bucket policy that grants `s3:GetObject` to `arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration`. Then add a CORS rule allowing `GET` and `HEAD` from `https://forge.coreweave.com`. CORS is the setting that lets the browser fetch the images. If objects use a customer-managed KMS key, that key's policy must also grant this role `kms:Decrypt` [S2].
- **GCS:** Give `wandb-integration@wandb-production.iam.gserviceaccount.com` the `roles/storage.objectViewer` role, and add the same kind of CORS rule [S2].

**Team setup**
1. Open `https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/settings`, go to **Reference buckets** and select **Add bucket** [S3].
2. Choose AWS or Google Cloud and enter the bucket name without the `s3://` or `gs://` prefix [S3].
3. Enter the key of one existing object, such as `photos/cat.png`. W&B reads it to check access and CORS. After that, links work for any object in the bucket [S3].
4. Optionally select **Test connection**, then select **Add bucket** [S3].

Screenshots won't display until the bucket is registered [S3]. Once it is, they show inline in the **Traces** view. If Weave can't find an object or the bucket isn't registered, you'll see the plain URI instead [S7].

# Reference media in your own bucket (BYOB) using Weave Op

> Render images and video that live in your own cloud bucket in Weave traces by logging their URIs, without importing the bytes into Weave.

Use this technique when the media you want to see in Weave already lives in your own bucket:

* Frames from a video pipeline.
* Screenshots from a browser agent.
* Images a model wrote to S3.

Instead of re-uploading those bytes into Weave, you log the object's URI as a string and Weave renders the image or video inline from your bucket. Only the URI is sent to Weave; the bytes stay in your bucket. Logging a 2 GB video costs the same as logging its path.

This is different from logging media with the [Content API](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/core-types/media.md#contents-api), which reads the bytes and stores them in Weave.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This is a Weave feature and is separate from [platform BYOB (secure storage connector)](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/secure-storage-connector.md), which backs W\&B artifact and run storage. Reference media buckets are configured per team and only need read access.

sources.heading: Configure your bucket
sources.text:
## Configure your bucket

Grant W\&B read access to the bucket and allow the browser to fetch objects with CORS.

When you view a trace, W\&B presigns a short-lived download URL for each referenced object. Grant the W\&B integration principal read access on the bucket so presigning can succeed. This is read-only access for inline rendering.

**AWS S3**

1. Apply a bucket policy that grants the W\&B integration principal `s3:GetObject`. Save the following as `bucket-policy.json`, replacing `[YOUR-BUCKET]` with your bucket name:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Id": "WandBAccess",
     "Statement": [{
       "Sid": "WandbAccess",
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration"},
       "Action": "s3:GetObject",
       "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::[YOUR-BUCKET]/*"
     }]
   }
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket [YOUR-BUCKET] --policy file://bucket-policy.json
   ```

2. Apply a CORS configuration so the app can fetch objects in the browser. Save the following as `cors.json`:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   {
     "CORSRules": [{
       "AllowedHeaders": ["*"],
       "AllowedMethods": ["GET", "HEAD"],
       "AllowedOrigins": ["https://forge.coreweave.com"],
       "ExposeHeaders": ["ETag"],
       "MaxAgeSeconds": 3000
     }]
   }
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   aws s3api put-bucket-cors --bucket [YOUR-BUCKET] --cors-configuration file://cors.json
   ```

> [!NOTE]
>
> If an object is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, its key policy must also grant `arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration` `kms:Decrypt`. The bucket policy alone is not sufficient.

**Google Cloud Storage**

1. Grant the W\&B integration service account `roles/storage.objectViewer` on the bucket. Replace `[YOUR-BUCKET]` with your bucket name:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://[YOUR-BUCKET] \
     --member="serviceAccount:wandb-integration@wandb-production.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
     --role="roles/storage.objectViewer"
   ```

2. Apply a CORS configuration so the app can fetch objects in the browser. Save the following as `cors.json`:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   [{
     "origin": ["https://forge.coreweave.com"],
     "method": ["GET", "HEAD"],
     "responseHeader": ["ETag"],
     "maxAgeSeconds": 3000
   }]
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   gcloud storage buckets update gs://[YOUR-BUCKET] --cors-file=cors.json
   ```

At this point, Weight & Biases can read objects from your bucket, and the UI can fetch them in the browser.

sources.text:
## Register the reference bucket

Register the bucket in your team settings so Weave can presign and display referenced URIs.

1. Go to your team settings page (`https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/settings`).
2. In the **Reference buckets** section, select **Add bucket**.
3. Select your cloud provider (**AWS** or **Google Cloud**).
4. For the bucket name, enter `[YOUR-BUCKET]` only — without the `s3://` or `gs://` prefix.
5. For the object key, enter the key of an existing object in the bucket, for example `photos/cat.png` (the object key only, not a full URL). W\&B reads this one object to confirm it has read access and that CORS is configured correctly. This checks access only; once verified, presigning works for any object in the bucket.
6. Optionally, select **Test connection** to validate the configuration without saving.
7. Select **Add bucket** to save.

![The Add reference bucket dialog in team settings, with fields for the cloud provider, the bucket name, and an existing object key, plus Test connection and Add bucket buttons.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/add-ref-bucket.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=7ab906b46a48b51e085530aaaf1e47a4)

> [!WARNING]
>
> Until the bucket is registered, referenced URIs do not render. Registration is what lets Weave presign and display the object.

sources.heading: How it works
sources.text:
## How it works

Reference media rendering works in three steps:

1. You store a media object in your bucket, for example `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/frames/000123.png`.
2. You log that URI as a string value anywhere in a trace: an Op input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name does not matter.
3. When you open the trace, Weave resolves the URI to a short-lived [presigned URL](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/presigned-urls.md) and renders it inline. The file extension decides how it renders. Common image formats (such as `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) and video formats (such as `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.webm`) render inline. Other formats render as a download link.

Weave only resolves URIs that point at a bucket registered for your team. Supported schemes are `s3://` and `gs://`.

## How it works

Reference media rendering works in three steps:

1. You store a media object in your bucket, for example `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/frames/000123.png`.
2. You log that URI as a string value anywhere in a trace: an Op input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name does not matter.
3. When you open the trace, Weave resolves the URI to a short-lived [presigned URL](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/presigned-urls.md) and renders it inline. The file extension decides how it renders. Common image formats (such as `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) and video formats (such as `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.webm`) render inline. Other formats render as a download link.

Weave only resolves URIs that point at a bucket registered for your team. Supported schemes are `s3://` and `gs://`.

> Render images and video that live in your own cloud bucket in Weave traces by logging their URIs, without importing the bytes into Weave.

## Configure your bucket

Grant W\&B read access to the bucket and allow the browser to fetch objects with CORS.

When you view a trace, W\&B presigns a short-lived download URL for each referenced object. Grant the W\&B integration principal read access on the bucket so presigning can succeed. This is read-only access for inline rendering.

**AWS S3**

1. Apply a bucket policy that grants the W\&B integration principal `s3:GetObject`. Save the following as `bucket-policy.json`, replacing `[YOUR-BUCKET]` with your bucket name:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Id": "WandBAccess",
     "Statement": [{
       "Sid": "WandbAccess",
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration"},
       "Action": "s3:GetObject",
       "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::[YOUR-BUCKET]/*"
     }]
   }
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket [YOUR-BUCKET] --policy file://bucket-policy.json
   ```

2. Apply a CORS configuration so the app can fetch objects in the browser. Save the following as `cors.json`:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   {
     "CORSRules": [{
       "AllowedHeaders": ["*"],
       "AllowedMethods": ["GET", "HEAD"],
       "AllowedOrigins": ["https://forge.coreweave.com"],
       "ExposeHeaders": ["ETag"],
       "MaxAgeSeconds": 3000
     }]
   }
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   aws s3api put-bucket-cors --bucket [YOUR-BUCKET] --cors-configuration file://cors.json
   ```

> [!NOTE]
>
> If an object is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, its key policy must also grant `arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration` `kms:Decrypt`. The bucket policy alone is not sufficient.

**Google Cloud Storage**

1. Grant the W\&B integration service account `roles/storage.objectViewer` on the bucket. Replace `[YOUR-BUCKET]` with your bucket name:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://[YOUR-BUCKET] \
     --member="serviceAccount:wandb-integration@wandb-production.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
     --role="roles/storage.objectViewer"
   ```

2. Apply a CORS configuration so the app can fetch objects in the browser. Save the following as `cors.json`:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   [{
     "origin": ["https://forge.coreweave.com"],
     "method": ["GET", "HEAD"],
     "responseHeader": ["ETag"],
     "maxAgeSeconds": 3000
   }]
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   gcloud storage buckets update gs://[YOUR-BUCKET] --cors-file=cors.json
   ```

At this point, Weight & Biases can read objects from your bucket, and the UI can fetch them in the browser.

result.text:
## How it works

Reference media rendering works in three steps:

1. You store a media object in your bucket, for example `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/frames/000123.png`.
2. You log that URI as a string value anywhere in a trace: an Op input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name does not matter.
3. When you open the trace, Weave resolves the URI to a short-lived [presigned URL](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/presigned-urls.md) and renders it inline. The file extension decides how it renders. Common image formats (such as `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) and video formats (such as `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.webm`) render inline. Other formats render as a download link.

Weave only resolves URIs that point at a bucket registered for your team. Supported schemes are `s3://` and `gs://`.

You log each screenshot's bucket URI, meaning its address such as `s3://bucket/key`, as a plain string in a trace. Weave sends only the URI to its servers, and the image bytes stay in your bucket [S1]. This is different from the Content API, which reads the bytes and stores a copy in Weave [S1].

**What you log**
- The URI as a string anywhere in a trace: an op's input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name doesn't matter, and you don't need a content annotation [S4, S6]. An "op" is a function you decorate with `@weave.op` so Weave records its calls.
- Only `s3://` and `gs://` URIs work, and only for buckets registered to your team [S4].
- The file extension decides how the file is shown. `.png`, `.jpg` and `.gif` appear as images, and other formats appear as a download link [S4].

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

@weave.op
def record_screenshot(screenshot_uri: str) -> dict:
    return {"screenshot": screenshot_uri}

record_screenshot("s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/screens/step-001.png")
```
This follows the documented pattern [S6]. For agent applications, there is a separate guide for agent spans [S6].

**Before you start**
- Your deployment must support it: Multi-tenant Cloud, or preview on Dedicated Cloud and Self-Managed v0.84.0+ [S5].
- You need a CoreWeave Forge account with an API key, an S3 or GCS bucket you control with at least one object, and organization admin permission [S5].

**Storage setup (read-only access)**
When someone opens a trace, W&B creates a short-lived download link (a "presigned URL") for each object, so it needs read access to the bucket [S2].
- **S3:** Add a bucket policy that grants `s3:GetObject` to `arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration`. Then add a CORS rule allowing `GET` and `HEAD` from `https://forge.coreweave.com`. - **GCS:** Give `wandb-integration@wandb-production.iam.gserviceaccount.com` the `roles/storage.objectViewer` role, and add the same kind of CORS rule [S2].

# Reference media in your own bucket (BYOB) using Weave Op

> Render images and video that live in your own cloud bucket in Weave traces by logging their URIs, without importing the bytes into Weave.

Use this technique when the media you want to see in Weave already lives in your own bucket:

* Frames from a video pipeline.
* Screenshots from a browser agent.
* Images a model wrote to S3.

Instead of re-uploading those bytes into Weave, you log the object's URI as a string and Weave renders the image or video inline from your bucket. Only the URI is sent to Weave; the bytes stay in your bucket. Logging a 2 GB video costs the same as logging its path.

This is different from logging media with the [Content API](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/core-types/media.md#contents-api), which reads the bytes and stores them in Weave.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This is a Weave feature and is separate from [platform BYOB (secure storage connector)](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/secure-storage-connector.md), which backs W\&B artifact and run storage. Reference media buckets are configured per team and only need read access.

sources.heading: Configure your bucket
sources.text:
## Configure your bucket

Grant W\&B read access to the bucket and allow the browser to fetch objects with CORS.

When you view a trace, W\&B presigns a short-lived download URL for each referenced object. Grant the W\&B integration principal read access on the bucket so presigning can succeed. This is read-only access for inline rendering.

**AWS S3**

1. Apply a bucket policy that grants the W\&B integration principal `s3:GetObject`. Save the following as `bucket-policy.json`, replacing `[YOUR-BUCKET]` with your bucket name:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Id": "WandBAccess",
     "Statement": [{
       "Sid": "WandbAccess",
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration"},
       "Action": "s3:GetObject",
       "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::[YOUR-BUCKET]/*"
     }]
   }
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket [YOUR-BUCKET] --policy file://bucket-policy.json
   ```

2. Apply a CORS configuration so the app can fetch objects in the browser. Save the following as `cors.json`:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   {
     "CORSRules": [{
       "AllowedHeaders": ["*"],
       "AllowedMethods": ["GET", "HEAD"],
       "AllowedOrigins": ["https://forge.coreweave.com"],
       "ExposeHeaders": ["ETag"],
       "MaxAgeSeconds": 3000
     }]
   }
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   aws s3api put-bucket-cors --bucket [YOUR-BUCKET] --cors-configuration file://cors.json
   ```

> [!NOTE]
>
> If an object is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, its key policy must also grant `arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration` `kms:Decrypt`. The bucket policy alone is not sufficient.

**Google Cloud Storage**

1. Grant the W\&B integration service account `roles/storage.objectViewer` on the bucket. Replace `[YOUR-BUCKET]` with your bucket name:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://[YOUR-BUCKET] \
     --member="serviceAccount:wandb-integration@wandb-production.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
     --role="roles/storage.objectViewer"
   ```

2. Apply a CORS configuration so the app can fetch objects in the browser. Save the following as `cors.json`:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   [{
     "origin": ["https://forge.coreweave.com"],
     "method": ["GET", "HEAD"],
     "responseHeader": ["ETag"],
     "maxAgeSeconds": 3000
   }]
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   gcloud storage buckets update gs://[YOUR-BUCKET] --cors-file=cors.json
   ```

At this point, Weight & Biases can read objects from your bucket, and the UI can fetch them in the browser.

sources.text:
## How it works

Reference media rendering works in three steps:

1. You store a media object in your bucket, for example `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/frames/000123.png`.
2. You log that URI as a string value anywhere in a trace: an Op input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name does not matter.
3. When you open the trace, Weave resolves the URI to a short-lived [presigned URL](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/presigned-urls.md) and renders it inline. The file extension decides how it renders. Common image formats (such as `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) and video formats (such as `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.webm`) render inline. Other formats render as a download link.

Weave only resolves URIs that point at a bucket registered for your team. Supported schemes are `s3://` and `gs://`.

all_read_evidence.text:
## Configure your bucket

Grant W\&B read access to the bucket and allow the browser to fetch objects with CORS.

When you view a trace, W\&B presigns a short-lived download URL for each referenced object. Grant the W\&B integration principal read access on the bucket so presigning can succeed. This is read-only access for inline rendering.

**AWS S3**

1. Apply a bucket policy that grants the W\&B integration principal `s3:GetObject`. Save the following as `bucket-policy.json`, replacing `[YOUR-BUCKET]` with your bucket name:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Id": "WandBAccess",
     "Statement": [{
       "Sid": "WandbAccess",
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration"},
       "Action": "s3:GetObject",
       "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::[YOUR-BUCKET]/*"
     }]
   }
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket [YOUR-BUCKET] --policy file://bucket-policy.json
   ```

2. Apply a CORS configuration so the app can fetch objects in the browser. Save the following as `cors.json`:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   {
     "CORSRules": [{
       "AllowedHeaders": ["*"],
       "AllowedMethods": ["GET", "HEAD"],
       "AllowedOrigins": ["https://forge.coreweave.com"],
       "ExposeHeaders": ["ETag"],
       "MaxAgeSeconds": 3000
     }]
   }
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   aws s3api put-bucket-cors --bucket [YOUR-BUCKET] --cors-configuration file://cors.json
   ```

> [!NOTE]
>
> If an object is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, its key policy must also grant `arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration` `kms:Decrypt`. The bucket policy alone is not sufficient.

**Google Cloud Storage**

1. Grant the W\&B integration service account `roles/storage.objectViewer` on the bucket. Replace `[YOUR-BUCKET]` with your bucket name:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://[YOUR-BUCKET] \
     --member="serviceAccount:wandb-integration@wandb-production.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
     --role="roles/storage.objectViewer"
   ```

2. Apply a CORS configuration so the app can fetch objects in the browser. Save the following as `cors.json`:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   [{
     "origin": ["https://forge.coreweave.com"],
     "method": ["GET", "HEAD"],
     "responseHeader": ["ETag"],
     "maxAgeSeconds": 3000
   }]
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   gcloud storage buckets update gs://[YOUR-BUCKET] --cors-file=cors.json
   ```

At this point, Weight & Biases can read objects from your bucket, and the UI can fetch them in the browser.

all_read_evidence.text:
## How it works

Reference media rendering works in three steps:

1. You store a media object in your bucket, for example `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/frames/000123.png`.
2. You log that URI as a string value anywhere in a trace: an Op input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name does not matter.
3. When you open the trace, Weave resolves the URI to a short-lived [presigned URL](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/presigned-urls.md) and renders it inline. The file extension decides how it renders. Common image formats (such as `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) and video formats (such as `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.webm`) render inline. Other formats render as a download link.

Weave only resolves URIs that point at a bucket registered for your team. Supported schemes are `s3://` and `gs://`.

# Reference media in your own bucket (BYOB) using Weave Op

> Render images and video that live in your own cloud bucket in Weave traces by logging their URIs, without importing the bytes into Weave.

Use this technique when the media you want to see in Weave already lives in your own bucket:

* Frames from a video pipeline.
* Screenshots from a browser agent.
* Images a model wrote to S3.

Instead of re-uploading those bytes into Weave, you log the object's URI as a string and Weave renders the image or video inline from your bucket. Only the URI is sent to Weave; the bytes stay in your bucket. Logging a 2 GB video costs the same as logging its path.

This is different from logging media with the [Content API](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/core-types/media.md#contents-api), which reads the bytes and stores them in Weave.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This is a Weave feature and is separate from [platform BYOB (secure storage connector)](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/secure-storage-connector.md), which backs W\&B artifact and run storage. Reference media buckets are configured per team and only need read access.

result.text:
## Configure your bucket

Grant W\&B read access to the bucket and allow the browser to fetch objects with CORS.

When you view a trace, W\&B presigns a short-lived download URL for each referenced object. Grant the W\&B integration principal read access on the bucket so presigning can succeed. This is read-only access for inline rendering.

**AWS S3**

1. Apply a bucket policy that grants the W\&B integration principal `s3:GetObject`. Save the following as `bucket-policy.json`, replacing `[YOUR-BUCKET]` with your bucket name:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Id": "WandBAccess",
     "Statement": [{
       "Sid": "WandbAccess",
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration"},
       "Action": "s3:GetObject",
       "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::[YOUR-BUCKET]/*"
     }]
   }
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket [YOUR-BUCKET] --policy file://bucket-policy.json
   ```

2. Apply a CORS configuration so the app can fetch objects in the browser. Save the following as `cors.json`:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   {
     "CORSRules": [{
       "AllowedHeaders": ["*"],
       "AllowedMethods": ["GET", "HEAD"],
       "AllowedOrigins": ["https://forge.coreweave.com"],
       "ExposeHeaders": ["ETag"],
       "MaxAgeSeconds": 3000
     }]
   }
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   aws s3api put-bucket-cors --bucket [YOUR-BUCKET] --cors-configuration file://cors.json
   ```

> [!NOTE]
>
> If an object is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, its key policy must also grant `arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration` `kms:Decrypt`. The bucket policy alone is not sufficient.

**Google Cloud Storage**

1. Grant the W\&B integration service account `roles/storage.objectViewer` on the bucket. Replace `[YOUR-BUCKET]` with your bucket name:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://[YOUR-BUCKET] \
     --member="serviceAccount:wandb-integration@wandb-production.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
     --role="roles/storage.objectViewer"
   ```

2. Apply a CORS configuration so the app can fetch objects in the browser. Save the following as `cors.json`:

   ```json lines theme={"system"}
   [{
     "origin": ["https://forge.coreweave.com"],
     "method": ["GET", "HEAD"],
     "responseHeader": ["ETag"],
     "maxAgeSeconds": 3000
   }]
   ```

   Then apply it to your bucket:

   ```bash theme={"system"}
   gcloud storage buckets update gs://[YOUR-BUCKET] --cors-file=cors.json
   ```

At this point, Weight & Biases can read objects from your bucket, and the UI can fetch them in the browser.

result.heading: How it works
result.text:
## How it works

Reference media rendering works in three steps:

1. You store a media object in your bucket, for example `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/frames/000123.png`.
2. You log that URI as a string value anywhere in a trace: an Op input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name does not matter.
3. When you open the trace, Weave resolves the URI to a short-lived [presigned URL](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/presigned-urls.md) and renders it inline. The file extension decides how it renders. Common image formats (such as `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) and video formats (such as `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.webm`) render inline. Other formats render as a download link.

Weave only resolves URIs that point at a bucket registered for your team. Supported schemes are `s3://` and `gs://`.

Open the trace from the link that `weave.init()` prints. The referenced image or video renders inline in the **Traces** view. If Weave can't resolve a URI, for example because the object is missing or the bucket isn't registered, it shows the plain URI string.

![A referenced image rendering inline in the Weave Traces view, resolved from a bucket URI that points at an object in your own cloud bucket.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/traces-byob.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=1089bf820959dde0fd237d7cc8e239d2)

# Reference media in your own bucket (BYOB) using Weave Op

> Render images and video that live in your own cloud bucket in Weave traces by logging their URIs, without importing the bytes into Weave.

Use this technique when the media you want to see in Weave already lives in your own bucket:

* Frames from a video pipeline.
* Screenshots from a browser agent.
* Images a model wrote to S3.

Instead of re-uploading those bytes into Weave, you log the object's URI as a string and Weave renders the image or video inline from your bucket. Only the URI is sent to Weave; the bytes stay in your bucket. Logging a 2 GB video costs the same as logging its path.

This is different from logging media with the [Content API](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/core-types/media.md#contents-api), which reads the bytes and stores them in Weave.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This is a Weave feature and is separate from [platform BYOB (secure storage connector)](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/secure-storage-connector.md), which backs W\&B artifact and run storage. Reference media buckets are configured per team and only need read access.

Yes. Weave can show screenshots that already sit in your own S3 or Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket. You log each screenshot's bucket URI, meaning its address such as `s3://bucket/key`, as a plain string in a trace. Weave sends only the URI to its servers, and the image bytes stay in your bucket [S1]. This is different from the Content API, which reads the bytes and stores a copy in Weave [S1].

**What you log**
- The URI as a string anywhere in a trace: an op's input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name doesn't matter, and you don't need a content annotation [S4, S6]. An "op" is a function you decorate with `@weave.op` so Weave records its calls.
- Only `s3://` and `gs://` URIs work, and only for buckets registered to your team [S4].
- The file extension decides how the file is shown. `.png`, `.jpg` and `.gif` appear as images, and other formats appear as a download link [S4].

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

@weave.op
def record_screenshot(screenshot_uri: str) -> dict:
    return {"screenshot": screenshot_uri}

record_screenshot("s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/screens/step-001.png")
```
This follows the documented pattern [S6]. For agent applications, there is a separate guide for agent spans [S6].

**Before you start**
- Your deployment must support it: Multi-tenant Cloud, or preview on Dedicated Cloud and Self-Managed v0.84.0+ [S5].
- You need a CoreWeave Forge account with an API key, an S3 or GCS bucket you control with at least one object, and organization admin permission [S5].

**Storage setup (read-only access)**
When someone opens a trace, W&B creates a short-lived download link (a "presigned URL") for each object, so it needs read access to the bucket [S2].
- **S3:** Add a bucket policy that grants `s3:GetObject` to `arn:aws:iam::725579432336:role/WandbIntegration`. Then add a CORS rule allowing `GET` and `HEAD` from `https://forge.coreweave.com`. CORS is the setting that lets the browser fetch the images. If objects use a customer-managed KMS key, that key's policy must also grant this role `kms:Decrypt` [S2].
- **GCS:** Give `wandb-integration@wandb-production.iam.gserviceaccount.com` the `roles/storage.objectViewer` role, and add the same kind of CORS rule [S2].

**Team setup**
1. Open `https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/settings`, go to **Reference buckets** and select **Add bucket** [S3].
2. Choose AWS or Google Cloud and enter the bucket name without the `s3://` or `gs://` prefix [S3].
3. Enter the key of one existing object, such as `photos/cat.png`. W&B reads it to check access and CORS. After that, links work for any object in the bucket [S3].
4. Optionally select **Test connection**, then select **Add bucket** [S3].

Screenshots won't display until the bucket is registered [S3]. Once it is, they show inline in the **Traces** view. If Weave can't find an object or the bucket isn't registered, you'll see the plain URI instead [S7].

issues: The rendering rule is overstated. S4 gives `.png`, `.jpg` and `.gif` only as examples ("such as") of common image formats. It also says common video formats such as `.mp4`, `.mov` and `.webm` render inline. The answer instead treats those three image extensions as the full list and says every other format becomes a download link, which contradicts S4 for video and for other common image formats. Correction: say that common image formats (for example `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) and common video formats render inline, and that other formats render as a download link [S4].
